entries.title: Bounded degree alone does not give a connective limit [draft; pending w347]
entries.statement: There is an infinite connected tree of maximum degree three whose rooted self-avoiding-walk counts c_n satisfy liminf c_n^(1/n)=1 and limsup c_n^(1/n)=2. Use successive level-block lengths 2^(2^j), with one child in even blocks and two in odd blocks. Rooted scalar submultiplicativity already fails at c_1=c_2=1,c_3=2. This refutes a generic bounded-degree existence route, but the example is not a stationary iid percolation cluster of Z^2.
entries.proof_text:
Let c_n(o) count length-n self-avoiding walks from the root of an infinite spherically symmetric tree. At level l, all vertices have b_l children. Partition the levels into successive blocks of lengths L_j=2^(2^j), j=0,1,... . Give one child at every level in even blocks and two children in odd blocks. This is an infinite connected tree with maximum degree three.

Every self-avoiding root walk moves outward, so c_n(o)=product_{l<n} b_l. At the end N_j=sum_{h<=j} L_h, write B_j for the number of two-child levels among those N_j. Then log(c_{N_j}(o))/(N_j*log 2)=B_j/N_j. The earlier blocks have total at most j*L_{j-1}=j*sqrt(L_j), negligible relative to L_j. Along odd block ends this ratio tends to one; along even block ends it tends to zero. Since every ratio lies in [0,1],

    liminf c_n(o)^(1/n)=1,  limsup c_n(o)^(1/n)=2.

The exponential limit therefore does not exist even on an infinite connected bounded-degree graph. On the first three levels, c_1=c_2=1 but c_3=2, directly refuting scalar rooted submultiplicativity c_{n+m}(o)<=c_n(o)*c_m(o). This tree lacks the translation-stationary percolation structure of P0004 and is not a counterexample to that problem.

entries.title: Translation invariance proves the full-lattice boundary limit [draft; pending w347]
entries.statement: For the p=1 bond-percolation configuration on Z^2, let c_n(v) count length-n self-avoiding walks from v. Translation invariance and prefix splitting give c_{n+m}(0)<=c_n(0)*c_m(0). Thus c_n(v)^(1/n) has a common limit in [2,3] by Fekete subadditivity, independent of v. This boundary result does not prove the quenched limit for p in (p_c,1).
entries.proof_text: Translate each prefix endpoint to zero; the permitted suffixes inject into all length-m origin walks. This gives scalar submultiplicativity. Fekete applied to log c_n gives the limit. There are 2^n monotone northeast walks and at most 4*3^(n-1) walks without immediate reversal, giving the bounds. Translation preserves the counts.
